transcript:
Meeting: Command Deck + Culture Cadence - Redwood all-hands
Date: 2026-08-12 10:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Leadership + company

Auto-summary (AI generated): Quick-run through of top-level metrics, product priorities, reliability story, and changes to operating rhythm. Open Q&A with cross-team clarifications.

[00:00] Lena Park (CEO): Good morning, everyone. Uh, we'll kick off — thanks for joining. Quick framing: today's short deck, two big asks: one on cadence changes, and one on culture rituals. We're trying to keep this tight so teams can get back to ship.

[00:28] Marco Ruiz (CTO): Hi all. I'll start with the product and infra headlines. Latency p50 is holding steady at 220ms on hosted, with occasional spikes late-night last week that Devon will cover. Throughput is up 12% month-over-month thanks to the batching improvements. There was one incident — a cross-region redis failover that cascaded into a KV cache cold start. It looked like K-V cash TTLs were misapplied when we failed over, so the warmup caused a token spike.

[01:15] Devon Price (Head of Reliability): Yeah, to be clear, the failover scenario combined a rolling upgrade with an old config in one region. The KV cache rehydration path didn't fallback fast enough; we saw about 6 minutes of elevated latency and request errors for some Dedicated pools. Root cause: mismatch between the new autoscaler and legacy cache priming. We'll put postmortem in docs and recommend a short SLO tweak while we roll the fix.

[02:05] Jonah Kim (VP Eng): The mitigation is already in ship — we pushed a circuit-breaker and reworked the priming logic. Long term, it's about improving the canary process for infra changes. Also, we need clearer rollout playbooks when we touch Dedicated capacity young pools.

[02:42] Aisha Banerjee (Head of Product): From product side — priorities haven't shifted: 1) Host API stability and cost efficiency, 2) Dedicated capacity controls and faster autoscaling, 3) Private deployment edge cases (V-P-C and on-prem packaging). On the roadmap, we've bumped up the Dedicated observability features — per-route p99 tracing and token-cost attribution.

[03:30] Lena: Quick hiring note — hiring velocity has slowed slightly because of market competition. We prioritised senior infra hires. Aisha, can you speak to roles?

[03:44] Aisha: Sure. We're focusing on ML infra (two ICs), two infra engineers for autoscaling, and one product manager for Dedicated. That will unstick a number of initiatives. Recruiting is pushing pipelines; we'll need hiring managers to interview promptly.

[04:10] Eleanor Shaw (Head of People): On culture, we heard feedback about meeting fatigue. Proposal: tighten recurring syncs, introduce a company-wide 'Focus Friday' policy (no recurring internal meetings 1st hour), and a monthly optional demo slot for teams to showcase work. We want to respect deep work time without killing visibility.

[04:45] Maya Chen (DX): The optional demo slot would be an async-first recording, 30 minutes, focused, with a one-pager shared. We'll experiment for two months.

[05:12] Lena: Ok, let's open to Q&A.

[05:20] Speaker 7: Hi, quick question on Dedicated pricing. For customers running high throughput, are we leaning into lower unit costs or faster autoscale? The tradeoff impacts how we prioritize queuing and bin packing.

[05:41] Marco: Good question. We'll generally default to predictability for Dedicated customers — lower unit cost with reserved pools — but we also want burst policies. There's product work to make routing policy more explicit, e.g., route by cost tier vs latency tier.

[06:08] Speaker 3: Another question: after the incident, do we plan to change SLOs?

[06:18] Devon: Short answer yes — temporary SLO relaxation and a longer-term change to make our error budget calculations more conservative for Dedicated pools during upgrades. We'll post specifics.

[06:45] Jonah: Also, need better observability for private deployments — customers asking for audit logs and local tracing to troubleshoot. That ties into the Private product work Aisha mentioned.

[07:10] Lena: On cross-team OKRs — we want three measurable outcomes for the quarter: reduce p95 latency by 10% for common prompt shapes, cut token cost per unit by 8% via caching and quantization guidance, and ship Dedicated autoscale policies. Who owns the second?

[07:37] Aisha: Product + DX will collaborate — Maya will take lead with infra assistance. We'll set a baseline measurement and a biweekly check-in.

[08:02] Eleanor: A couple of culture asks: can we formalize recognition for cross-team work? Small things: a standardized shoutout mechanism in Slack, and a quarterly 'impact' microgrant for great infra work.

[08:28] Lena: Solid. We'll pilot the shoutout channel and microgrants.

[08:40] [09:00] — Rapid Q&A and smaller clarifications — examples below:

[09:00] Speaker 2: Will the Focus Friday apply to Customer-Facing teams?

[09:15] Eleanor: Customer-facing folks will be exempt for scheduled calls, but we'll push minimal internal meetings.

[09:40] Marco: One more infra note: we continue to invest in compilation and kernel selection improvements — that's a multi-quarter effort but will yield consistent p99 improvements once stable.

[10:05] Speaker 5: Any update on the SDK latencies? We saw a couple of regressions after the last release.

[10:20] Maya: We're rolling back the experimental buffer change in SDK v2.1. The rollback will be cut tonight; we'll monitor.

[10:38] Lena: Ok, closing the deck. Quick shoutouts?

[10:45] Jonah: Shoutout to the infra team for the fast circuit breaker and to recruiting for filling the Sr candidate pipeline — appreciated.

[11:05] All / Multiple: applause / thanks / yay

[11:20] Lena: Recap — action owners listed on the deck. Please review the post and sign up for follow-ups. We'll run a Dedicated roadmap deep dive next week; calendar invite from Marco. Thanks, everyone.

[11:38] Devon: Quick note — reliability follow-up will include a tabletop drill for failover scenarios; we'll invite engineers from Dedicated and Platform teams.

[11:50] Aisha: And product will publish a short decision doc on the Dedicated observability tradeoffs by Friday.

[11:58] Lena: Meeting ends. Thanks.

Notes about transcript: minor transcription errors present (SAML sometimes transcribed as S A M L, KV cache as K-V cash), occasional speaker attribution confusion for 1-2 interjections.
